question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

7 × 2 + 4 - 6 ÷ 3 = 12
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebadc30a979bf1a7e953d20901c3e7953c575296c0e0bb4af8a458ec3a64ab2c.png] 

Given statement : 7 × 2 + 4 - 6 ÷ 3 = 12

According to the question, after interchanging the signs:

So,

__
 
• Option - (1) : × and -​

Given statement : 7 × 2 + 4 - 6 ÷ 3 = 12

After interchanging:

7 - 2 + 4 × **6 ÷ 3**__ = 12

7 - 2 + __**4 **____**× 2**__ = 12

__**7 + 8**__ - 2 = 12

__**15 - 2**__ = 12

13 ≠ 12 (LHS ≠ RHS)

__
 
• Option - (2) : = and ×

Given statement : 7 × 2 + 4 - 6 ÷ 3 = 12

After interchanging:

7 = 2 + 4 - **6 ÷ 3**__ × 12

7 = 2 + 4 - __**2 × 12**__

7 = __**2 + 4**__ - 24

7 = 6 - 24

7 ≠ -18 (LHS ≠ RHS)

__
 
• Option - (3) : - and +

Given statement : 7 × 2 + 4 - 6 ÷ 3 = 12

After interchanging:

7 × 2 - 4 + **6 ÷ 3**__ = 12

__**7 × 2**__ - 4 + 2 = 12

__**14 + 2**__ - 4 = 12

__**16 - 4**__ = 12

12 = 12 (LHS = RHS)

__
 
• Option - (4) : - and =

Given statement : 7 × 2 + 4 - 6 ÷ 3 = 12

After interchanging:

**7 × 2**__ + 4 = __**6 ÷ 3**__ - 12

__**14 + 4**__ = __**2 - 12**__

18 ≠ -10 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, "Option - (3)" is the correct answer.
